title: What the Bank Took
logline: A family in a northern town watches a repossession agent walk out with the one vehicle they scrimped years to buy, and no argument brings it back.
human_question: What happens to wanting when the thing you finally got is taken away again?

premise.story: The day a family's vehicle, bought after years of saving and loan repayments, is repossessed over missed payments: the arguments, the paperwork, the neighbours who gather, and the family's life the next morning without it.
premise.place: A family home and yard in a northern town, on the day of a repossession.
premise.experience: The ordinary morning of a family interrupted; official calm against private loss; the strange quiet of a yard with an empty space in it.

concept_links.why: The vehicle is precisely the concept's own subject: a thing held with real attachment, wanted badly and finally owned, and then handled with the flat, professional indifference of someone whose job is to take it away [C004-M:L13] [C004-M:L17].

What was a source of pleasant feeling becomes a source of pain the moment it changes hands, which is the concept's own account of pleasant feeling carrying the seed of loss when conditions turn [C032-P:L117].

what_camera_could_observe: Paperwork and an agent's practised, neutral manner
The yard and the family's routine the next morning, changed
what_must_be_real: A genuine repossession, with the family's full, informed consent to be filmed during a difficult and legally sensitive event. No dispute staged or resolved for the camera.

possible_arc.opening: An ordinary morning, before anyone arrives.
possible_arc.turn: The agent arrives with the paperwork, and the family's wanting meets a wall.
possible_arc.ending_open: The vehicle leaves, or the family finds a way to keep it a little longer. Reality decides.

position_hint: closing candidate: a direct, unmistakable image of the group's arc closing on wanting refused, lost or taken, ready to hand off into a story of what that loss turns into.

requirements: A family genuinely facing repossession, willing to be filmed through a legally and emotionally sensitive event
Cooperation or at least non-obstruction from the lender or agent involved
Careful legal and editorial handling of a real financial dispute

suggestions.name: A town in the Vavuniya area
suggestions.why: A regional town plausible for this kind of story; no specific family or case is known.
suggestions.access_notes: This event would need to be found in progress or agreed in advance with a real family; it cannot be arranged for the camera.
suggestions.verify: No family, lender or case has been identified. This entire idea depends on finding a real, willing situation.

risks: High sensitivity: financial hardship and shame must never be exploited
Legal complexity around filming a repossession
The family's dignity and consent must be protected above the story
drop_if: No family experiencing this can be found who freely and fully consents to being filmed
Filming would worsen the family's legal or financial situation

connections.note: One family loses what it finally had; another loses what it never quite got. Both are wanting meeting a wall.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
